channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: The chip rout is funding the Dow Jones Industrial Average's record chase
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just short of 52,900 on Tuesday, higher by close to 700 points and 1.3%, roughly 450 points beneath the record it set in the first week of July. Taken alone, that reads as a broad risk rally.

item.title: The Euro is not rallying, the British Pound Sterling is being demoted
item.description: The Euro is on track for its eighth gain in nine sessions against the Pound, and the explanation that would normally cover a run of that length is not available.

item.title: Silver loses ground as hopes for US-Iran deal improve risk appetite
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $57.40 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 1.7% on the day. The white metal is under pressure as the US Dollar (USD) loses some strength and investors reduce their exposure to safe-haven assets ahead of the Federal Reserve's (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bears target the 200-day SMA after losing the $80 mark
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil extends its decline on Tuesday after falling 9% the previous day following a pause in attacks between the United States and Iran. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $77.90, down nearly 4% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar Index eases from tops, back to 101.30 ahead of Fed
item.description: The Greenback, when tracked by the US Dollar Index (DXY), abandons the area of monthly peaks and recedes toward the 101.30 zone on turnaround Tuesday.

item.title: Euro skyrockets amid softer US confidence
item.description: EUR/USD trades higher near the 1.1400 area on Tuesday, gaining around 0.3% as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following softer United States (US) consumer-confidence data. The US Dollar Index falls toward 101.30, helping the Euro extend its recovery.

item.title: Gold: Hawkish Fed delays Gold recovery path – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch and Thu Lan Nguyen note that the Gold price has dropped nearly 30% from its January record as higher real yields and hawkish Federal Reserve expectations weigh on the metal.

item.title: Oil: Weakens on deal hopes and fragile flows – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Brent has sold off sharply as US–Iran strikes pause and President Trump signals a “good chance” of a deal. They stress that flows through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, as well as Black Sea exports, remain critical.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds onto losses after Bullock keeps further rate hikes on the table
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near the 0.6970 area on Tuesday, falling around 0.3% as the Australian Dollar (AUD) comes under pressure despite hawkish remarks from Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock.

item.title: British Pound Sterling has nothing to say in front of two central banks
item.description: The Pound trades near 1.3300 in the New York morning, effectively flat on a session that has run barely 30 pips between a floor a shade above 1.3250 and a ceiling fractionally above the 1.3300 handle.

item.title: British Pound: Bearish reversal extends before BoE – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report GBP/USD is extending its bearish reversal toward early-July levels as markets scale back Bank of England (BoE) tightening expectations. September pricing has been cut and cumulative hikes by December reduced.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD sits out the panic it was built for
item.description: Gold trades near $4,020 in the Tuesday New York morning, down roughly 1.4% on a session that started near $4,075 and never built a bid.

item.title: $4,000: Gold’s key support faces a crucial Fed test
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Tuesday, pressured by a firmer US Dollar (USD), even as Oil prices extend their pullback on hopes of an end to the US-Iran war.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA keeps hike option alive – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock signaled a possible rate hike at the August 10–11 meeting, stressing inflation is still too high and productivity weak.

item.title: Canadian Dollar benefits from softer US Dollar despite lower Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD trades near 1.4105 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 0.14% on the day, though the pair remains close to its recent highs as traders refrain from taking aggressive positions ahead of the Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Knife-edge policy risks surprise – ING
item.description: ING’s Padhraic Garvey expects the Federal Reserve (Fed) to leave rates unchanged at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, with odds seen around 60:40 for no move.

item.title: Euro holds near recent lows as Fed interest rate decision looms
item.description: EUR/USD struggles for direction on Tuesday as traders avoid taking directional positions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate decision on Wednesday while closely monitoring US-Iran developments.

item.title: Euro: Pressured by softer ECB expectations – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight a softer Euro (EUR), with EUR/USD drifting toward the mid-1.13s and levels last seen in May 2025.

item.title: US CB Consumer Confidence Index eases to 90.8 in July
item.description: US consumer sentiment loses some momentum in July, as the Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index recedes to 90.8 from June’s 92.2 (revised from 91.2).

item.title: Why hot Australian inflation could reignite the Reserve Bank of Australia hike debate
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is balancing stickier-than-expected domestic inflation against broader global market volatility.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Weak performance tied to carry and Gold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that the Swiss Franc’s (CHF) underperformance since the February 2026 Iran shock reflects both low-yield carry dynamics and sensitivity to Gold prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA pause risk weighs on Aussie – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that Australian Dollar (AUD) is underperforming after Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock balanced a hawkish bias with a message of patience, noting easing domestic demand and labour conditions.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Limited upside for CAD against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note USD/CAD is trading near fair value around 1.4115, with the Canadian Dollar (CAD) constrained by wide short-term rate differentials versus the Dollar.

item.title: British Pound: Political risks and BoE stance shape outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses British Pound (GBP) prospects around UK welfare reform, shifting voter polls and the upcoming Bank of England (BoE) decision. Foley highlights how PM Burnham’s fiscal choices and intra-Labour tensions could affect gilts and the Pound.

item.title: Trump downplays escalation risks while warning Iran against breaking agreements
item.description: In an interview with Fox News, US President Donald Trump said that Pickaxe Mountain, an Iranian underground nuclear site, is not a big problem, adding that the United States (US) is now in a very strong position with Iran.

item.title: Copper: Tight supply underpins constructive outlook – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Copper has extended its July gains as easing Middle East tensions lift sentiment. They point to tight physical conditions, low inventories and firm Chinese import demand as key supports.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Scenarios into FOMC – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Eugene Leow notes that investors remain cautious on upcoming FOMC decisions, with markets pricing a 34% chance of a July hike and nearly full odds for September.

item.title: Euro nears three-week high against British Pound on UK fiscal concerns, BoE outlook
item.description: EUR/GBP holds firm on Tuesday, extending its recovery from the more than one-year low touched earlier this month as diverging monetary policy expectations between the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of England (BoE), along with UK fiscal concerns, weigh on the British Pound (GBP).

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles as firm US Dollar keeps NZD/USD pinned
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5770 on Tuesday at the time of writing, slightly lower on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains pressured by the firm US Dollar (USD), which continues to benefit from safe-haven demand amid persistent geopolitical tensions.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average drops to 15K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has further cooled in mid-July. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 15K jobs per week in the four weeks ending July 11.
